claims.title: Coast woven into Horn of Africa trade
claims.summary: The shores of the Bab-el-Mandeb form part of the ancient commercial world of the Horn, exchanging aromatics, ivory and other goods with Egypt and southern Arabia; the wider region is linked to the fabled Land of Punt.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1000bce-coast-woven-into-horn-of-africa-trade, claim TL:DJI:event:1000bce:coast-woven-into-horn-of-africa-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Islam reaches the Red Sea coast
claims.summary: Islam spreads to the coast of the Horn within the first century of the faith, carried by merchants and migrants from Arabia across the narrow strait.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-650-islam-reaches-the-red-sea-coast, claim TL:DJI:event:650:islam-reaches-the-red-sea-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zeila a centre of Islam and trade
claims.summary: The port of Zeila, just south of present-day Djibouti, grows into one of the oldest Muslim towns of the Horn and a hub of Red Sea commerce serving the interior.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-900-zeila-a-centre-of-islam-and-trade, claim TL:DJI:event:900:zeila-a-centre-of-islam-and-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sultanate of Ifat dominant on the routes
claims.summary: The Walashma-ruled Sultanate of Ifat, with Zeila as its principal port, commands the trade routes between the Ethiopian highlands and the Red Sea, spreading Muslim political power into the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1285-sultanate-of-ifat-dominant-on-the-routes, claim TL:DJI:event:1285:sultanate-of-ifat-dominant-on-the-routes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ifat broken by Ethiopia; rise of Adal
claims.summary: The Ethiopian emperor Amda Seyon defeats Ifat; the Sultanate of Adal succeeds it as the leading Muslim power contesting the Christian highlands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1332-ifat-broken-by-ethiopia-rise-of-adal, claim TL:DJI:event:1332:ifat-broken-by-ethiopia-rise-of-adal, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Adal's invasion of the highlands
claims.summary: Adal forces under Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi ('Gran') invade Christian Ethiopia, the high point of the coastal Muslim states' power before Adal's later decline.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1529-adal-s-invasion-of-the-highlands, claim TL:DJI:event:1529:adal-s-invasion-of-the-highlands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Local Afar and Issa polities
claims.summary: After Adal's decline the region fragments into Afar sultanates such as Tadjoura and Raheita and Issa Somali clan territories, the local powers France would later engage.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1700-local-afar-and-issa-polities, claim TL:DJI:event:1700:local-afar-and-issa-polities, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: France buys the anchorage of Obock
claims.summary: France purchases the anchorage of Obock on the Gulf of Tadjoura from local Afar sultans, its first foothold on the coast.

sources.label: Historique des relations franco-djiboutiennes jusqu'à l'indépendance (1977)
sources.publisher: La France à Djibouti (French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1862-france-buys-the-anchorage-of-obock, claim TL:DJI:event:1862:france-buys-the-anchorage-of-obock, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Lagarde extends French control
claims.summary: Léonce Lagarde is sent to oversee French interests; treaties with Afar and Somali rulers over the following years extend a French protectorate around the Gulf of Tadjoura.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1884-lagarde-extends-french-control, claim TL:DJI:event:1884:lagarde-extends-french-control, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Djibouti city
claims.summary: Lagarde founds the port-city of Djibouti on the southern shore of the gulf, with a superior harbour, and transfers the administration there from Obock.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1888-founding-of-djibouti-city, claim TL:DJI:event:1888:founding-of-djibouti-city, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Colony of French Somaliland created
claims.summary: A French decree constitutes the holdings as the colony of the Côte française des Somalis (French Somaliland), with Djibouti as its capital, replacing Obock as the seat of government.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1896-colony-of-french-somaliland-created, claim TL:DJI:event:1896:colony-of-french-somaliland-created, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Franco-Ethiopian Railway begun
claims.summary: Construction starts on the railway from the port of Djibouti toward the Ethiopian interior, the project that will define the colony's economy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1897-franco-ethiopian-railway-begun, claim TL:DJI:event:1897:franco-ethiopian-railway-begun, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Railway reaches Addis Ababa
claims.summary: The line is completed to Addis Ababa, giving landlocked Ethiopia its main outlet to the sea and confirming Djibouti as the entrepôt for Ethiopian trade.

sources.label: 100-year-old Ethiopia's French-built railway remains vital for residents

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1917-railway-reaches-addis-ababa, claim TL:DJI:event:1917:railway-reaches-addis-ababa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Djibouti rallies to Free France
claims.summary: After a period under Vichy control and blockade during the Second World War, the colony joins the Free French forces.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1942-djibouti-rallies-to-free-france, claim TL:DJI:event:1942:djibouti-rallies-to-free-france, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reorganised as an overseas territory
claims.summary: French Somaliland becomes an overseas territory of the French Union, gaining representation in Paris and limited local institutions amid the wider decolonisation of Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1946-reorganised-as-an-overseas-territory, claim TL:DJI:event:1946:reorganised-as-an-overseas-territory, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First referendum keeps ties to France
claims.summary: Voters in French Somaliland choose to remain within the French Community rather than join independent Somalia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1958-first-referendum-keeps-ties-to-france, claim TL:DJI:event:1958:first-referendum-keeps-ties-to-france, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Renamed Territory of the Afars and the Issas
claims.summary: A second, disputed referendum again favours association with France; the territory is renamed the French Territory of the Afars and the Issas.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1967-renamed-territory-of-the-afars-and-the-issas, claim TL:DJI:event:1967:renamed-territory-of-the-afars-and-the-issas, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence referendum passes
claims.summary: A final referendum returns an overwhelming majority for independence from France.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1977-independence-referendum-passes, claim TL:DJI:event:1977:independence-referendum-passes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Republic of Djibouti proclaimed
claims.summary: Djibouti becomes independent, the last French territory on mainland Africa to do so; Hassan Gouled Aptidon becomes the first president.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1977-republic-of-djibouti-proclaimed, claim TL:DJI:event:1977:republic-of-djibouti-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: One-party state established
claims.summary: President Gouled makes Djibouti a one-party state under the People's Rally for Progress (RPP).
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1981-one-party-state-established, claim TL:DJI:event:1981:one-party-state-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Civil war with the FRUD rebellion
claims.summary: The Afar-based Front for the Restoration of Unity and Democracy launches an insurgency in 1991; the civil war runs until a 1994 accord with the movement's moderate wing largely ends it.

sources.label: Front for the Restoration of Unity and Democracy

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1991-civil-war-with-the-frud-rebellion, claim TL:DJI:event:1991:civil-war-with-the-frud-rebellion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ismail Omar Guelleh becomes president
claims.summary: Gouled steps down and his nephew and chief of staff Ismail Omar Guelleh wins the presidency, beginning a long tenure that continues to the present.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-1999-ismail-omar-guelleh-becomes-president, claim TL:DJI:event:1999:ismail-omar-guelleh-becomes-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Final FRUD peace accord
claims.summary: President Guelleh presides over a final peace agreement with the hardline FRUD faction led by Ahmed Dini, formally ending the decade-long conflict.

sources.label: Djibouti: Peace agreement addresses Afar discontent

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-2001-final-frud-peace-accord, claim TL:DJI:event:2001:final-frud-peace-accord, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: China opens its first overseas base
claims.summary: China inaugurates its first overseas military base in Djibouti, joining French, US (Camp Lemonnier), Japanese and other forces and confirming the country's role as a hub of foreign military presence.

sources.label: People's Liberation Army Support Base in Djibouti

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Djibouti: A small Horn of Africa republic at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway, from ancient trade and early Islam through French Somaliland to a coveted hub of world shipping and foreign military bases.", terralore.co/country/DJI/chronicle#ev-2017-china-opens-its-first-overseas-base, claim TL:DJI:event:2017:china-opens-its-first-overseas-base, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
